After a second straight loss in ACC play, Louisville looks to get back on track when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Ky., on Friday at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville prediction and college football picks expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:58 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's amazing how fast two weeks can change things. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. How To Watch Florida State vs Louisville Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, KY – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Florida State Will Win So what did Florida State do against Virginia to generate all of this excitement? The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. Louisville 38, Florida State 30 Latest Consensus Line: Louisville -3.5, o/u: 59.5 ATS Confidence (out of 5) : 4 Must See Rating (out of 5) : 3.5 Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Louisville Cardinals | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 8, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football Can FSU win their third straight against Louisville to go 4-2 on the season? The Florida State Seminoles are traveling to Kentucky to meet the Louisville Cardinals for another ACC Friday Night Lights game at the L&N Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. and will be televised on ESPN. Florida State (3-2, 1-1 ACC) leads the all-time series 18-6, including a 7-3 record at Louisville (2-3, 1-2 ACC). FSU has won the last two games against the Cardinals, including a 16-6 victory in the 2023 ACC Championship Game and a 35-31 win in their most recent regular-season matchup in Louisville in 2022. The Cardinals are 4-6 against the Seminoles since joining the ACC in 2014. The Cardinals took a second straight defeat last Saturday, dropping a 31-28 contest at NC State. All three of Louisville’s losses this season have come by three points. Seven of its last eight losses dating back to 2024 have come by three points or less. The Cardinals have eight touchdowns of 50 yards or more this season, the most of any team in FBS. Five different Louisville players have scored a touchdown of 50 yards or more this season. Louisville is averaging 486 yards per game, second-best in the ACC, and has 37 plays of 20 yards or more through five games, tied with Indiana for the most in the country. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has rushed for 158 yards on the ground this season and is tied for fifth nationally among quarterbacks with six rushing touchdowns. In the first five games, Kienholz has completed 96 of 139 of his passes for a 69.1 completion percentage, 9 touchdowns with 1 interception, and is averaging 278 yards per game. The Cardinals rushed for 231 yards in the loss at NC State, with Miami native Isaac Brown rushing for 125 yards on nine carries, his 12th 100-yard game. Keyjuan Brown leads the Cardinals in rushing with 367 yards, averaging 9.7 yards per carry. Wide receiver Tre Richardson leads the Cards with 28 receptions for 445 receiving yards and has scored three touchdowns (2 receiving, 1 rushing). The three touchdowns Richardson has scored this season have been 30, 62, and 38 yards. Of his 33 offensive touches this season, 19 have gone for at least 10 yards and nine have covered 20 yards or more. The only player in the ACC with more plays of 20 yards or more is Miami’s Malachi Toney. Tight end Jaleel Skinner has hauled in 14 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns through five games. Skinner is one of just 20 players in the FBS to have multiple 60-yard plays from scrimmage and the only tight end to do it, scoring touchdowns from 61 and 69 yards. Overall, the Cardinals rank 17th in the nation in total offense (486 yards/game), 22nd in scoring offense (38.6 points/game), T-24th in passing offense (287.4 yards/game), and 38th in rushing offense (198.6 yards/game). Similar to the Seminoles, Louisville’s defense is struggling. Linebacker J.T. Capers leads the defense with 38 tackles, followed by defensive back Kaleb Beasley with 35 tackles and 3 interceptions. The Cardinal defense ranks 125th in total defense, giving up 423 yards per game, 130th in passing yards allowed (267 yards/game), and 113th in scoring defense (29.2 points/game). Florida State is coming off its most impressive win of the season, notching a 38-7 win over Virginia last Saturday. Quarterback Ashton Daniels’ five touchdowns in the victory set an FSU record, now placing him third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns and ranked 3rd with 15.87 yards per completion, while also leading the ACC in rushing scores and in yards per completion. His 183 passing yards, career-high 136 rushing yards, and five touchdowns against Virginia make him the only FBS player since 1995 to reach those marks in a game. FSU 38, Virginia 7: Seminoles dominate Cavaliers in all three phases in blowout win FSU’s improving defense now ranks 103rd in the nation, giving up 385 yards/game, 127th in passing defense (266 yards/game), and ranked T-98th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 41% of the time on third-down attempts. However, the Noles’ defense has been decent at stopping opponents behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 3.4 sacks per game for 8th best in the nation, and 20th in tackles for loss with 7.2 TFLs per game. Louisville junior wide receiver Lawayne McCoy played two seasons at Florida State before transferring this year to Louisville. In two years with the Seminoles, McCoy played in 20 games with 33 receptions for 448 yards and three touchdowns. Florida State Director of Football Strategy/Offensive Assistant Gabe Fertitta was a quality control assistant at Louisville during the 2021 season. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Louisville Cardinals Florida State is trending as a 3.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 59.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-1, 2-3 ATS) Welp. Last week’s game is certainly making me at least consider the possibility that I was being a bit harsh about this team. Somehow, FSU enters this game with a better record than Louisville. The Seminoles haven’t won a road game since 2023, but this Louisville team is coming off back-to-back losses to Wake Forest and NC State and has a knack for making a lot of mistakes. I’m still not convinced that FSU has turned over a new leaf, but as a show of faith, I’ll give them some benefit of the doubt. Florida State 31, Louisville 27 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-1 ) FSU took down a genuinely good team in Virginia, and looking back on the Alabama game, we were probably the best punch against them up to this point that ended up losing. I’m going to go out on a pretty rickety limb here and say that FSU finally ends its 1,000+ day road losing streak and defeats Louisville. Louisville’s run defense is allowing 156.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 92nd nationally. If Wisner and company can establish the run, or if Daniels can go for five touchdowns again, it’ll be a fun time for the Seminoles. Give me FSU to pull off the “upset.” FSU 41, Louisville 31 NoleThruandThru (season record: 5-0) Louisville 41, FSU 38 Jessi Wynn (season record: 3-0) Florida State enters the matchup with momentum from a two-game winning streak, including a dominant 38-7 win over Virginia. The Seminoles looked strong on both sides of the ball, with the offense finding success in both the running and passing games. FSU has struggled on the road, but I think the confidence from this winning streak will carry over. Noles 39, Louisville 32 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-1) Like everyone else, I have to reconsider how I think the next three games will go for Florida State after last week’s win against Virginia. The Seminoles ripped through the UVA offensive line for 10 sacks, ran the quarterback effectively, and played their cleanest game in what seems like forever. They also get a break, even though they travel on a short week, by facing a reeling Louisville team that has lost two in a row. Plus, for whatever reason, FSU has played well against the Cards the last few times they have met. However, one win isn’t enough for me to trust this team, especially on the road. The defense will have its hands full against Jeff Brohm’s offense, and one week does not mean all the problems are solved. FSU keeps this game close, but a bad turnover and a back-breaking touchdown drive result in a loss. Take UL to cover and the over. UL 34, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 4-0) I need to see it to believe it when it comes to FSU on the road; Louisville’s pass rush is fierce, so a successful formula is a lot of QB power and play-action shot. Louisville is bloodied and a mess on defense, but FSU hasn’t won a road game since 2023, so…. Louisville 35 , FSU 31 Jon Marchant (season record: 4-1 ) Louisville looked like a good, solid squad, but they keep losing close games. FSU, meanwhile, looked like a completely different team from what we’ve seen since 2023. Will the real FSU please stand up? Can FSU win this game? Yes. But Friday night on the road is tough. Louisville 28 , FSU 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 4-1) Friday’s game might be a battle of which team has the ball last. There should be a decent amount of points scored on both sides, though FSU could always “struggle.” In the end, I think UL has more firepower, and old friend Lawayne McCoy makes some key plays to secure the Louisville win. Louisville 45, FSU 38 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-1, 4-1 ATS) My, how the tables turn. All of a sudden, Louisville is the team in disarray, while Florida State is coming off its best game since beating Alabama to open the 2025 season. FSU’s offense has looked very good for large stretches the last few weeks, and most of those stretches occur when Norvell simplifies the number of reads Ashton Daniels has to process. If that continues, the ‘Noles should have no problem scoring 24+ points, as they have in every game this season. Will 24 be enough? Not likely. Even in back-to-back losses, UL has put up 27 and 28 points, respectively. I need to see more than one week of good defense to believe FSU will hold UL to a season low on a short week in Louisville. So now the question becomes: can Florida State outscore the Cardinals? Call me crazy, but I say yes! FSU 34, Louisville 30 Frank DaNole (season record: 3-2) These two teams are similar in that both have decent offenses while fielding defenses that leave a lot to be desired. This will be the second game when everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are only 3.5-point underdogs as the road team for a reason. Vegas knows it, and the Seminoles know it. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed last week. The Seminoles may not dominate at all three positional units for the entire game, but in the end FSU will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Cardinal opponents. FSU Seminoles 38, Louie’s Flock 31 Perry Kostidakis (season record: 3-2, 3-2 ATS) If there was ever a time for FSU to continue its success with its front seven, it’s this game. The Cardinals’ offensive line has struggled this season, giving up two sacks (81st in the country) and 6.4 tackles for loss (121st) per game. Defensively, Louisville has struggled as much as Florida State has — its 266.8 passing yards per game allowed ranks 130th in the country (FSU is 127 with 265.6) — so even if the defensive turnaround on the Seminoles’ end was fugazi, I do have confidence in their ability to put up points after another successful offensive showing. What are the things that give me pause? away.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

Defensive back Antonio Watts, punter Jacob Baker, wide receiver Montavin Quisenberry, tight ends Travis Egan and Hamilton Atkins, offensive linemen Bryten Close and Sam Secrest, and defensive lineman Sam Dawson won't play. Defensive back TJ Banks, running back Keyjuan Brown, offensive lineman Cason Henry, and defensive lineman Daylen Russell are questionable. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, defensive back Koen Entringer, defensive linemen AJ Green and Joshua Donald, plus offensive linemen Ellis McAdoo and Anwar O'Neal are probable. away.blurb: Florida State and Louisville have released their initial injury reports ahead of Friday night's clash, according to Yahoo Sports . The Seminoles are without key receivers and defensive backs, while the Cardinals have their starting quarterback listed as probable. This report matters because it tells you exactly who will step onto the field when the teams meet at 7 PM on ESPN. Fans need to know the starting lineup before the game starts. The Seminoles are dealing with a long list of players who will not be available. Running back Samuel Singleton Jr. is out, along with wide receiver Devin Carter. The defense loses three defensive backs: Karson Hobbs, Jamari Howard, and Zae Thomas. Linebacker Blake Nichelson and Jordan Crutchfield are also out. The team is missing several other players on the defensive side of the ball, including Daylen Green and Noah LaVallee. These absences force coach Mike Norvell to shuffle his depth chart significantly before kickoff. On the positive side, linebacker Mikai Gbayor and Karon Maycock are probable. Defensive back Antonio Cromartie Jr. and punter Daniel Hughes are also expected to play. However, defensive lineman Darryll Desir is questionable after not playing last week. The team released this list on Tuesday night to give fans a clear view of the roster status. Louisville has good news regarding their offense. Starting quarterback Lincoln Kienholz is listed as probable after being questionable earlier in the week. He started against NC State last week, so he is familiar with the game flow. The Cardinals also have defensive back Koen Entringer and lineman AJ Green listed as probable. However, they are without defensive back Antonio Watts and tight end Travis Egan. Starting quarterback Lincoln Kienholz's status is the biggest story for Louisville fans heading into the game. The Cardinals are also missing several other key players. Running back Keyjuan Brown is questionable, along with offensive lineman Cason Henry. Defensive lineman Daylen Russell is also in the questionable group. The team is missing a large chunk of their offensive line depth with Bryten Close and Sam Secrest out. Wide receiver Montavin Quisenberry is also out for the game. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. Indiana's Turbo Richard runs for a touchdown against Western Kentucky. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Hoosiers' offense ranks 14th nationally, averaging 489.6 yards and 44.2 points per game. I thought two weeks ago we ran to the ball harder than we did last week. I was disappointed in that. I want people to talk about our defense as the hardest-playing group in the country. So, we’ve got to play extremely hard.” “The backs have a high break tackle ratio,” he continued. “We’ve got to tackle their backs at an elite level, which is something we’re going to work on today.” Anthony Jones Jr. makes a tackle against Michigan State. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Huskers allowed several explosive plays against the Terrapins last week, which is a major concern heading into a matchup against the likes of Indiana. Aurich mentioned Dwayne McDougle's game-changing 81-yard pick-six in the second quarter against Maryland. “He looked at that look all week, and so he had an opportunity to execute something he’s done" Aurich said. And the Cornhuskers are off to a good start, coming in undefeated through five games, but still unranked and beating teams that are nothing like the caliber of opponent that they'll see this weekend in the Hoosiers and their 21-game win streak. What do experts think of this week's matchup? For that, let's turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Indiana remains the expected favorite against Nebraska on the road, but in what could be a close game. SP+ predicts that Indiana will defeat Nebraska by a projected score of 31 to 24 and will win the game by an expected margin of 7.7 points on the road. The model gives the Hoosiers a strong 69 percent chance of outright victory. SP+ is a "tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency" that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring "the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football." How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Huskers catch the Hoosiers? There's a lot to like about the Cornhuskers' offense right now. It ranks top 15 in points per game, scoring at least 31 in every game, and 48 in three out of five outings. Indiana hasn't looked its usual self until laying a 47-15 beating on Rutgers a week ago, and it still boasts one of the most potent rushing attacks in the country, tacking on 253 yards on the ground on average. Nebraska has performed admirably well against its competition thus far, but the discrepancy between what the Hoosiers put on the field compared to those other teams is too great to ignore. Home field keeps the Huskers in it for a while, but Indiana has the firepower to pull away by double digits. What happens? Indiana beats Nebraska and covers the spread. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 Mon, October 5, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College Football can be odd. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. How will Nebraska perform against a rated team? Can they break the streak and knock off a ranked opponent? Would the rebuild fully be "on" if such a feat were to occur? Regardless of our collective thoughts on the outcome of the game, Vegas isn't counting on it. The line on FanDuel Sportsbook has Indiana as a 7.5-point favorite, marking the first time this season that Nebraska entered as the underdog. The over/under for the contest is 52.5 points. Bet your heart, but do so responsibly. Big Noon Kickoff between Nebraska and Indiana is Saturday at 11:00am Central, LIVE from Memorial Stadium, on Fox!

picks.headline: Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment
picks.blurb: Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 6:51 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska enjoyed a few terrific seasons over the last 25 years, but for all intents and purposes, the historic superpower hasn't been in the national title hunt since losing to Miami in the BCS Championship to end the 2001 season. There's still plenty of work to do after this week, but beating the defending national champion – and putting an end to Indiana's 21-game winning streak – would be just the moment the program has been waiting for to show that it's headed in the right direction. Indiana hasn't been the dominant version of last year, but it's still unbeaten, it's about as tuned up as it can be, and it got its first road game out of the way with a 47-15 win over Rutgers. Yeah, this might be Nebraska's moment. It's also Curt Cignetti's moment to prove that for the Hoosiers, it's business as usual. Indiana vs Nebraska Quick Hits The Hoosiers get three home games in the next four after this, but Ohio State is up next, the road date is at Michigan, and then Minnesota and USC come to Bloomington. Nebraska goes on the road for three games in the next four dates, with a trip to Oregon before a week off to get ready for Washington. Indiana won 56-7 in 2024, but the Huskers are 6-1 in the series before that going back to a Hoosier win in 1959. How To Watch Indiana vs Nebraska Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, NE – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Indiana Will Win As you'd expect from one of the best coached teams in all of sports, Indiana doesn't mess up. It has only turned the ball over once, it's third in the nation in fewest penalties, and no one does a better job of not putting itself in tough situations. It might not be that Nebraska needs to force mistakes and can win this straight up, but it has a way of pulling away in games, helped by the takeaways. On the flip side, the Huskers were flagged 16 times in the win over Maryland and have committed the most penalties of any Big Ten team so far. Why Nebraska Will Win The Hoosiers have only been stress-tested once in the 29-23 win over Northwestern, and that was partly because Wildcat quarterback Aidan Chiles was accurate with the passing game. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea might not be Drew Brees, but he's hitting 66% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and just two picks. This has to be about the Nebraska offensive line, though. The Huskers are taking over games with the running game pushing until the dam breaks, and then games turn into routs. Indiana isn't Maryland or Bowling Green, but Michigan State is a tough-as-nails team that was the only team that held the Huskers to under 200 yards, and it still lost by 18. Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines Can Nebraska get close to 40 carries? Part of the problem against Indiana is that teams have to give up on the run because it doesn't work. Only North Texas has been able to get past 66 yards this season, and it's also the only team that ran more than 35 times. North Texas also lost 52-16. The energy of the moment will carry the Huskers to a solid first half, but they won't be able to pull away. Eventually, the Nebraska run defense will start to buckle, the IU pass rush will get to Colandrea, and the hype for the Ohio State game will start about 30 seconds after the final gun. home.blurb: Rule was labeled as doubtful in NU's initial availability report Wednesday. He remained there Thursday before moving up to questionable Friday. His return would bolster a running back room with an alarmingly low amount of career production. After being upgraded from questionable to probable, he appears set to return against the Terps. That would give the Huskers a key piece in both their passing and return games. If he sits this one out, more catches could be in store for Quinn Clark and Keelan Smith. Isaiah Mozee and Andrew Marshall are options as punt returners. The surprising news came Thursday when junior running back Mekhi Nelson was added to the availability report as questionable. That status stayed the same on Friday. Nelson's availability would provide a significant boost for the Huskers on the ground against Maryland. With Jamal Rule also questionable, NU could enter Saturday's contest without their two most productive backs. Isaiah Mozee, listed as a co-No. 1 on the depth chart with Rule and Nelson, has 31 carries for 149 yards this season, plus three receptions for 37 yards. Backups Kwinten Ives, Vincent Genatone and Conor Booth have combined for 10 carries for 49 yards and three receptions for 38 yards. Arizona's first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod's squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: "There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don't think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn't looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering." It's to no one's surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What's been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona's defense will try to neutralize this? "We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn't realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn't what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games." Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? "I think it's fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don't blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage." The Mountaineers' defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? "In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can't get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It's rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley's reputation as a sort of 'mad scientist' on defense could be part of the problem. It's really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn't matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here." How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? "After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I've seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod's first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it's humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn't want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around." Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. "We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home."

picks.headline: Arizona football at West Virginia score predictions
picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football at West Virginia Mountaineers score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 8, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Rich Rodriguez was Arizona’s coach from 2012-17, during which time he went 43-35 and reached bowl games in five of six seasons. Since parting ways with RichRod, the Wildcats have gone 42-54 and played in two bowl games, those coming in the last three seasons. When Arizona (4-1, 1-1 Big 12) takes on West Virginia (3-2, 0-2) on Saturday morning it will mark the first time since 1992 it is facing a former head coach. The UA went 2-4 against Larry Smith , their coach from 1980-86, while he was at USC. How will the Wildcats do on the road against their former coach? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Arizona wins 35-31 It’s a tale of two dramatically different offenses. Arizona has the highest pass completion percentage (72.6) in the Big 12 on the third most attempts (179). Only eight teams in the country are better. Its 299.8 yards per game are the second most passing yards in the conference and 19 th in FBS. As for West Virginia, it’s ranked 15 th in the league and 121 st in the country in completion percentage. It is last in the conference in pass attempts at just 88. Its 178 ypg are also last in the Big 12. That ranks 117 th in FBS. The Mountaineers don’t defend the pass very well, either. They’re allowing 288.2 ypg, suggesting that Arizona could easily meet its average this week. That’s also last in the Big 12. Meanwhile, Arizona is giving up 75 ypg less at 213.2. WVU makes up for that by having the 3 rd ranked rushing offense in the country with 294 ypg on the ground, almost twice as many as Arizona’s 151.6 ypg. That’s a problem the Wildcats conquered just last week when Cincinnati came to town. The Bearcats came to Tucson averaging 270 ypg on the ground. Arizona held them to a season low of 74. None of the Bearcats’ runs went for more than 21 yards after breaking off 53-yard gains against both Miami (OH) and Kansas State the previous two weeks. The shortest “big run” they had prior to that was 31 yards in their season opener. The Wildcats also showed their defensive prowess on the ground against BYU, even if it didn’t result in the win. The Cougars average 235.5 rushing ypg, which is good for 16 th in the country. UA held them almost 90 yards under that at 248 in week two. BYU may lose some of its rushing luster over the next month with LJ Martin injured, but that doesn’t take away from Arizona’s effort against a full-strength Cougar running attack. Can Arizona reproduce that in a game that is across the country and likely has some extra emotional baggage for the WVU head coach? From a statistical standpoint, it’s definitely within the realm of possibility. While WVU doesn’t defend Arizona’s strength very well, the Wildcats do defend the Mountaineers’ strength well. UA has the third best rushing defense in the Big 12, allowing just 79 ypg. That comes in at 11 th in the country. Opponents average just 2.97 yards per rushing attempt. The negatives for Arizona are the travel, kickoff time, and the general emotion that’s likely to be on the other sideline. Stats say the Wildcats could win, but those things might make it closer than it would otherwise be. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 31- 28 Traveling to the Eastern Time Zone for a noon kickoff that’s really 9 a.m. for the visitors from Tucson makes this a trickier game to pick than it might appear on the surface. First, the opponent. West Virginia has been inconsistent at home under Rich Rod and its last game in Morgantown resulted in a 41-24 loss to Oklahoma State. The Mountaineers are in desperation mode after starting 0-2 in Big 12 play following last week’s crushing loss at Iowa State. Rich Rod indicated postgame that his defensive coordinator is having trouble fixing what’s broken. It’s safe to say West Virginia players and coaches are feeling the heat at the moment, and a third straight loss would a message for what direction the program is heading under Rodriguez. I think Arizona’s defensive game plan will go a long ways in determining the outcome of the game. If Danny Gonzales and his staff put forth a plan to stymie the Mountaineers rushing attack, then the Wildcats should leave with a hard-earned win. Considering how well last week went, I’m going to ride with Danny G and Co. until proven otherwise. Adam Green — Arizona wins 38 -24 Before the season started I had this game as a loss for Arizona. Much like my colleague Juan below, I felt like the Cats traveling across the country to face a RichRod offense — without even knowing the kickoff time — would be too much to handle. Then Arizona obliterated Cincinnati and West Virginia’s defense has shown to be, well, offensive. Understanding that Arizona may have some struggles without any of its starting receivers, I’m thinking the Cats should still have little trouble moving the ball and putting up points in this one. The only real question is if Danny Gonzales’ defense will be up to the task of slowing down an offense that, when it’s right, is incredibly difficult to stop. If Arizona can limit turnovers and create long fields for the Mountaineers there should be just enough opportunity to put some distance between the teams on the scoreboard, and given the early kickoff we should have a pretty good idea early on if this one is going to go the Wildcats’ way. Juan Serrano — West Virginia wins 35-27 I had this game marked down as a loss in my preseason record prediction. I was called crazy on social media for this prediction but now it is not looking so unrealistic that Arizona could lose on Saturday. This line of thinking is not due to the Wildcats not playing well or anything like that because through five games they have looked solid. It’s more so due to the fact that the Mountaineers are better than most people thought they would be. I saw West Virginia’s improvement coming and thought it could present an issue for Arizona. Fans in Tucson know just how much former head coach Rich Rodriguez loves to run the football, and this season he has his Mountaineers as the third best rushing attack in the country. Danny Gonzales ’ defense was up to the task last week against Cincinnati, but this is a whole new challenge. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a difference maker and can be dangerous both on the ground and through the air. I believe the secondary’s discipline will be tested in a major way this week, and will struggle. Noah Fifita will need to execute an efficient offensive performance to more than likely keep up with West Virginia on the scoreboard. If the run game can continue progressing as it has over the last two weeks, then Arizona could possibly control the clock. However, I believe that Rodriguez will have his guys motivated to play extremely hard after two very tough losses. The former coach of the Wildcats will get a little bit of payback on Saturday, and West Virginia will earn it’s first conference win of the year and move to 2-0 overall against Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 38-21 I would be lying if I said that Morgantown was an easy place to play. Even so, there’s one glaring issue for West Virginia, their terrible defense. They haven’t faced an offense quite like Arizona and a QB like Noah Fifita . Last week, we saw what the Arizona offense can be when it is actually humming. And it looks great, even with three starting wide receivers out due to injury. If the offensive line has a good game, like I think they will, the running game will be able to establish some momentum and Noah will be able to pick the leaky Mountaineer secondary apart. Defensively, I think this game will be a challenge for Danny Gonzales. It would be silly to think otherwise. However, much like the offense, last week showed us what the defense can do when it’s operating on high octane. Gonzales’s crew played their most physical game and shut down a great Cincinnati rushing attack. I don’t think they’ll be able to shut down Rich Rodriguez’s run game, but I predict they will be able to disrupt it enough to degrade the offense. Michael Hawkins Jr. is a stud in the run game, but he isn’t much of an issue through the air. Arizona proved they can negatively impact a mobile quarterback last week, and I expect similar success this Saturday. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 38-34 Like Washington State, this is another game that I picked Arizona to lose prior to the season. But that was before I saw just how bad West Virginia’s defense is, and it’s bad. If the Wildcats don’t score more than 30 points in this game it’s because of their own mistakes, not for lack of opportunities. As good as the UA defense has been, and it’s been really good particularly against the run, to expect to shut down RichRod’s rushing attack is foolish. The man knows how to scheme a ground game, and if quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. can also complete some passes this will be a shootout. It will all come down to Noah Fifita and how he gels with the retooled receiving corps. West Virginia, meanwhile, is 3-2 overall and still searching for its first conference victory after dropping back-to-back games against Oklahoma State and Iowa State. The Mountaineers' latest loss was a wild 45-42 shootout in Ames. There's also an obvious storyline on the West Virginia sideline, where former Arizona head coach Rich Rodriguez will face his old program. Rodriguez coached the Wildcats from 2012-17 before eventually returning to Morgantown for his second stint leading the Mountaineers. Can Arizona build off its impressive win over Cincinnati, or will West Virginia get its first Big 12 victory of the season at home? Here's everything you need to know about Arizona vs. West Virginia , including the latest odds, our biggest question and our prediction and pick for Saturday's Week 6 matchup. The Biggest Question: Can West Virginia's Defense Stop Anything? This West Virginia defense is just horrible. They gave up 577 yards to Iowa State last week, and are allowing a Big 12-worst 456 yards per game, which is 50 more yards per game than any other Big 12 team. They're dead last in passing and rushing yards allowed per game, and second-worst in points allowed per game. The Mountaineers are 100th in the nation in net yards per play (offense minus defense), and rank dead last in defensive efficiency in the league. OK, you get the point. So what is Rich Rodriguez and Zac Alley changing ahead of Saturday? It's not clear. But something needs to change. West Virginia vs. Arizona Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 35, West Virginia 31 The West Virginia Mountaineers are going to be desperate to avoid an 0-3 start in Big 12 play. They have the running game to keep this thing competitive, however, Arizona's front seven is underrated. One week after Cincinnati rushed for over 200 yards vs. Kansas State, they only mustered 74 yards on 28 carries for 2.6 yards per carry vs. Arizona. I don't believe Arizona will have that level of success vs. this WVU rushing attack, that has been the most-potent in the Big 12, but they'll do enough. And if Arizona can jump out to a lead and force Michael Hawkins Jr. to try and win a game through the air, that's a recipe for success. The only concern I have for Arizona is the travel and early kick at 12:00 p.m. CT, which will be a 9:00 a.m. kick for Arizona's body clock. Those games are always tough. However, if you're worried you're on an island with Arizona, don't be. The Wildcats are attracting 91% of the money wagered and have been bet up from -3 to -3.5 , indicating that both recreational and larger bettors are backing Arizona. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.blurb: "We're at a point where we're going into conference play and we know we've got to play better," Hall told us at his weekly media conference. "We've not played our best yet. That's a negative, but also a positive that our best is still out there. You should get better as the season goes on....We feel like we're a much better football team right now than we were last time we talked to you (two weeks ago)," Expect the highly anticipated return of last year's breakout running back Jamauri McClure . The then-freshman sensation rushed for 540-yards, though really being used from about the midway point in the year on. He averaged 6.5-yards every time he touched the ball in 2025. McClure was injured during Fall practice getting surgery on his left foot to repair damage done. He's been sidelined all this year, with the Wave targeting the American opener as his season debut. Receiver Zycarl Lewis , who was hurt during the Duke game, is set to return as well, recovering from a leg injury. Though Hall listed both tight end Ty Thompson and linebacker Chris Rodgers as doubtful for Saturday, fans should not plan on either of them contributing this weekend. Thompson is nursing a leg injury that has forced him to miss extended time, and Rodgers has a foot injury that is putting the star backer on the sidelines for the foreseeable future. Tulane Prepares for Army Option, Welcomes Back 2025 Star RB from Injury Skip to main content On SI The Tulane football team opens the defense of its American Conference 2025 championship on Saturday with a trip to West Point to visit the United States Military Academy. Kickoff from Michie Stadium is set for 11:00 a.m. CT and can be seen on the CBS Sports Network. After a bye week to rest up and prepare, Green Wave head coach Will Hall is feeling good about his squad's preparedness. "The advantages of when our bye week fell is it is right smack dab in the middle of our season," Hall shared Tuesday. "We had five weeks of fall camp, then four games. That's nine weeks. Now we've got a bye week and eight games left. So, it's right in the middle. It is right before conference play and it's right before we play an option team. I think those are advantages The league opener is like a new season for Hall and his team, as they get ready for what is essentially a restart to their season. "We know how important it is to get off on the right foot and be 1-0 in conference play," Hall said Tuesday, "so our young men are taking that very seriously. But also we all want to play (well) for us and I want us to play (well) for our players. I want our players to play better, so in turn they get more touches and get more accolades for themselves and they get the the harvest for all the work they've put in. You can see it. away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

That's a negative, but also a positive that our best is still out there. You should get better as the season goes on....We feel like we're a much better football team right now than we were last time we talked to you (two weeks ago)," Expect the highly anticipated return of last year's breakout running back Jamauri McClure . The then-freshman sensation rushed for 540-yards, though really being used from about the midway point in the year on. He averaged 6.5-yards every time he touched the ball in 2025. McClure was injured during Fall practice getting surgery on his left foot to repair damage done. He's been sidelined all this year, with the Wave targeting the American opener as his season debut. Receiver Zycarl Lewis , who was hurt during the Duke game, is set to return as well, recovering from a leg injury. Though Hall listed both tight end Ty Thompson and linebacker Chris Rodgers as doubtful for Saturday, fans should not plan on either of them contributing this weekend. Thompson is nursing a leg injury that has forced him to miss extended time, and Rodgers has a foot injury that is putting the star backer on the sidelines for the foreseeable future. Tulane Prepares for Army Option, Welcomes Back 2025 Star RB from Injury Skip to main content On SI The Tulane football team opens the defense of its American Conference 2025 championship on Saturday with a trip to West Point to visit the United States Military Academy. Kickoff from Michie Stadium is set for 11:00 a.m. CT and can be seen on the CBS Sports Network. After a bye week to rest up and prepare, Green Wave head coach Will Hall is feeling good about his squad's preparedness. "The advantages of when our bye week fell is it is right smack dab in the middle of our season," Hall shared Tuesday. "We had five weeks of fall camp, then four games. That's nine weeks. Now we've got a bye week and eight games left. So, it's right in the middle. It is right before conference play and it's right before we play an option team. I think those are advantages The league opener is like a new season for Hall and his team, as they get ready for what is essentially a restart to their season. "We know how important it is to get off on the right foot and be 1-0 in conference play," Hall said Tuesday, "so our young men are taking that very seriously. But also we all want to play (well) for us and I want us to play (well) for our players. I want our players to play better, so in turn they get more touches and get more accolades for themselves and they get the the harvest for all the work they've put in. You can see it. picks.blurb: Texas vs Oklahoma Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Vaughn Dalzell Tue, October 6, 2026 at 10:20 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement NFL College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Red River Rivalry is back in the Cotton Bowl for another round of #1 Texas (4-0) versus Oklahoma (2-2)! This season's version showcases the No. 1 team in the country and an extra week of preparation for both teams as they had a bye. The game has the lowest total of the week at 39.5 points, so oddsmakers are expecting the defenses to dictate the day. Texas snuck out a win at Tennessee (20-17), but also blew it late with a touchdown and onside kick recovery by the Vols to give Tennessee a chance to win. On a positive note, the Longhorns defense had a day. Texas recorded 10 sacks and 12 TFL at Tennessee with a few more taken away because of penalties. It waa a dominant effort as Texas allowed 221 total yards (151 pass, 70 rush) and 4 -of-16 mark on third downs. Arch Manning had a quiet day going 14-of-19 for 201 yards, one interception, and a season-low zero touchdowns. Oklahoma is in a bad spot entering Week 6, but have a monumental opportunity to get back in the playoff hunt if they upset the No. 1 team in the country. The Sooners offense has failed to score more than 14 points in the last three games and failed to cross 300 total yards in all three games. Against Michigan and New Mexico, Oklahoma's defense kept them in the game with 23 total points allowed. John Mateer has thrown four interceptions in his last three games and has yet to record a rushing touchdown on the season. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Texas vs Oklahoma Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 3:30 PM Eastern Site: Cotton Bowl City: Dallas, TX TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Texas vs Oklahoma The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Texas Longhorns (-325), Oklahoma Sooners (+260) Spread: Texas -8.5 (-110) Total: 39.5 points #1 Texas Longhorns Head Coach: Steve Sarkisian 2026 Record: 4-0 (1-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 33.2 (T-55th) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.2 (11th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 2nd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 22nd The Texas Longhorns Offense: Texas had a season-low 262 yards and 61 rushing yards (1.7 ypc) against Tennessee and went 3-of-12 on third downs. The Longhorns committed 11 penalties for 115 yards in that game, which didn't get any better have 8 for 85 against UTSA. It will be interesting to see what changes are made for the Texas offense off the bye week, but it's obvious the Longhorns are trending in the wrong direction offensively. Texas Player to Watch on Offense: QB Arch Manning Arch Manning is coming off his worst statistical performance of the season. He's had some up and down performances despite Texas' success like 195 yards versus Ohio State with a large chunk coming in the fourth. Manning had 200 total yards versus Tennessee and no touchdowns with one interception. Manning has tossed a pick in three out of four games and was sacked a season-high six times against the Vols. Manning went 21-of-27 for 166 yards and one touchdown against Oklahoma last year, plus 34 rushing yards on four carries (one sack). The Texas Longhorns Defense: Texas was incredible against Tennessee on defense. The Longhorns grabbed a season-high 10 sacks and 12 TFL, plus held the Vols to 4-of-12 on third downs. It's wild to think Texas has 15 sacks on the season, so it'll be interesting to see if that pressure rolls over following the bye week or if that was a one-off performance and more of a credit to how bad Tennessee's line is. Oklahoma has a team total of 14.5, so Texas is expected to keep the Sooners out of the end zone all but two times. Last year, Texas allowed six points to Oklahoma and earned five sacks, seven TFL, and three interceptions. Texas Player to Watch on Defense: EDGE Colin Simmons Last year, Colin Simmons had 2.5 of the five sacks against John Mateer and he's coming in hot. Simmons had a program-record 5.5 sacks versus Tennessee! Simmons has 7.5 sacks on the season and has a three-game sack streak on his hands. The future first round pick will certainly be double-teamed more often than not against Oklahoma this weekend. Oklahoma Sooners Head Coach: Brent Venables 2026 Record: 2-2 (0-1) Offensive Points Per Game: 22.0 (109th) Defensive Points Per Game: 16.0 (T-24th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 3rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 13th The Oklahoma Sooners Offense: The Oklahoma offense had its roughest test of the year when it was smacked by Georgia (41-13). The Sooners turned the ball over four times, went 2-of-14 on third downs, posted 296 yards, and back-to-back games under 70 rushing yards. On the year, Oklahoma's offense ranks 122nd in success, 120th in rushing success, and 132nd in passing success. The Sooners rank 56th in team passing efficiency, tied-52nd in red zone offense (88.9%), and 109th in third-down offense (34%). Texas will be a tough draw. Oklahoma Player to Watch on Offense: QB John Mateer The 2026 season hasn't worked out how John Mateer and Oklahoma thought it would. Matter has tossed four picks in his last three games and has a 8:4 TD to INT ratio entering Week 6. Mateer has yet to record a rushing touchdown this year, which is wild considering he posted 15 in 2024 and 8 in 2025. Mateer was sacked three times against Michigan and Georgia, and will face another front seven with elite pressure rates in Texas. Last year, Mateer threw three interceptions against Texas and was sacked five times. The Oklahoma Sooners Defense: The Oklahoma defense will have to have a day to remember if they want to win this game, but it's possible. Oklahoma's defense ranks third in third-down defense (23.1%), fourth in passing yards allowed (122.5), second in red zone defense (60%), and 42nd in rushing yards allowed (115.5). Oklahoma has nine sacks in the last three games and did force Georgia into two turnovers. Oklahoma Player to Watch on Defense: DB Omarion Robinson Omarion Robinson grabbed the first interception for the Sooners defense of the season against Georgia. Texas has won three of the last four games in this rivalry after losing four straight from 2018 to 2021.
