No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 8, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. By James Parks | October 7, 2026 One of college football’s great rivalry games renews this weekend as the Red River Shootout finds No. 1 ranked Texas facing off against Oklahoma in a critical test for both sides, if for very different reasons just a month into the 2026 season. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. What do the analytics department think of this week’s matchup? For that, let’s turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction: Can Arch Beat the Sooners' Defense? Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may not come as a surprise that the Longhorns are getting the favorite treatment against the Sooners, and by a decent margin, too. SP+ predicts that Texas will defeat Oklahoma by a projected score of 27 to 17 and will win the game by an expected margin of 9.9 points in the process. The model gives the Longhorns a very strong 73 percent chance of victory, one of the biggest discrepancies of any game this weekend. SP+ is a “tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency” that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring “the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football.” How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Longhorns defend their No. 1 ranking? Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) in action during the game against the UTEP Miners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images That’s a different question. Even with a Texas win, its place atop the AP poll could be in danger anyway as pollsters may be more impressed with what happens between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama as they face off in primetime. A big win over the Sooners could sway enough voters to stay at No. 1 , and everything looks like it should go the Longhorns’ way. Even with questions around Arch Manning’s continued development at the quarterback position. Sure, Texas is 4-0 and Manning looks much better than this time last year, but he has also clearly still not performed to expectations, either. Arch is a decent 63 percent passer but is making some curious decisions and doesn’t look completely at ease in the pocket against better-quality fronts. Against an Oklahoma defense that, despite everything, remains one of college football’s best – 4th against the pass, top 25 in scoring, and 3rd in third-down conversions – Manning could get seriously rattled early. But the Longhorns still have an advantage of their own on defense. They have battery of elite pass rushers who can wreck OU’s blockers, shrink the pocket, and get at John Mateer on a regular basis. That should give the Texas offense enough chances to separate and pull away late. Horns by 10. What happens? Texas beats Oklahoma, and covers the spread. away.headline: Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again
away.blurb: Well, this week's message is along that exact same vein, with the Horns' head coach denying to provide any additional context ahead of releasing the first availability report of the week, which comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday evening. Both were listed as "OUT" on the final availability report for Week 4 , alongside defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman. For now, one could hope (and reasonably assume, based on Sarkisian's message about getting healthier) that at least one of those players is ready for, or close to ready for, action in the rivalry game. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.headline: Oklahoma vs Texas: Key players listed on Wednesday Availability report
home.blurb: Most notable is that the guy who was supposed to start at left tackle, Michael Fasusi, doesn't look like he'll be available again this week. He started for the Sooners against UTEP but has missed the last three games with a shoulder injury. Fasusi is doubtful for the Red River Showdown. Also in question is the status of starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis. Pierre-Louis was listed as questionable going into Saturday. Joining the ranks of the unavailable this week are Xavier Robinson and Jacobe Johnson. Johnson suffered an injury during the loss to Georgia. Why Robinson isn't available is anyone's guess. He didn't get much playing time against the Bulldogs, logging just three snaps after getting nine snaps the week before against Michigan. Along with Fasusi, who is doubtful, are reserve backup tight end Trynae Washington and backup offensive lineman Fred Hinton. Washington has been a piece of Oklahoma's short-yardage formations, lining up in the backfield as a fullback for the Sooners. Their presence on the availability report is just another week where the Sooners will have question marks along the offensive line. Names to watch as the week moves along include linebacker Cole Sullivan, wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, safety Michael Boganowski, and tight end Jack Van Dorselaer. The Sooners need a spark this week if they want to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners are 1-3 against the Texas Longhorns under Brent Venables, and the offense hasn't scored a touchdown against their Red River rivals since 2023. Missing key members of the offensive line and the tight end room doesn't bode well for the Sooners' chances this Saturday. Even redshirt junior quarterback Dante Moore could rest some more after suffering a concussion in the victory at the USC Trojans on Sept. 26. He was at the first practice this week, wearing a helmet and shoulder pads, according to coach Dan Lanning. Moore's next possible opponent would be the No. 21 UCLA Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten) , who are one of the three remaining undefeated Big Ten Conference programs. UCLA at Oregon's Updated Betting Odds The Week 6 matchup with the Southern California foe has Oregon still as a nearly two-touchdown favorite. According to FanDuel , the spread stands at 11.5. The Ducks' moneyline is -480 and the Bruins' is +360. The over/under is set at 58.5. The last time these two former Pac-12 Conference opponents met was in 2024, resulting in a 34-13 victory for Oregon in Pasadena, California. UCLA leads the all-time record, 33-40, dating back to 1928. The CBS matchup starts at 12:30 p.m. PT on Oct. 10 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon . Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana When speaking to the media back on Sept. 30, Lanning was quick to talk about the similarities that he has seen from the Bruins to last season's Big Ten and national champion, the Indiana Hoosiers. “They got some players that can play ball. Their running backs are as good as anyone who will go against them this year. They have a lot of players that came with them. And again, why I draw some comparisons to Indiana: a lot of guys that traveled with their coach right to the next stop.” First-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney brought offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy, defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, and fifth-year running back Wayne Knight along with him to sunny California after the James Madison Dukes of the Sun Belt Conference made the College Football Playoff last season. Their memorable run came to an end in the first round after a 51-34 loss to the Ducks in the Pacific Northwest on Dec. 21, 2025. “Extremely well-coached team," Lanning continued on about this year's Bruins. "You got two coordinators who were with him before, so they've been together for a while. They have a lot of continuity from that standpoint. They're running the ball as well as anybody in college football.” Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Even the challenges that senior Nico Iamaleava presents through his aggressiveness on quarterback scrambles. On Oct. 5, Lanning reiterated to the media just how effective Chesney's offense is without an efficient passing game. "I would argue they have explosive runs; anytime you can run the ball in the end zone, I think they have more rushing touchdowns this year than they've had in the last two years combined," stated Lanning. Knight is one of the top ball carriers in the nation. He has already collected 445 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns (tied for the third-most in the sport). Slowing the star back down is the key to an Oregon winning effort over that confident unit in the backfield. "Against the run, I think we do a good job stopping runs between the tackles," Lanning explained back on Sept. 30. "However, we give up some big runs around the outside, and we need to do a better job defending and adjusting to those plays." picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. McElroy picked against Oregon in Week 4, taking USC 34-31 before the Ducks won by 14 at the Coliseum. UCLA and Oregon kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Loading recommendations... picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. picks.blurb: Predicting Big Ten football scores in Week 6: UCLA looks for statement win over Oregon - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 6 of the college football season has arrived, and as usual, there are some Big Ten games to keep an eye on. It will begin on Friday night when Iowa travels to the West Coast to take on Washington. The Huskies have dropped two games and would love to win over the No. 20 Hawkeyes. There is another big matchup brewing for 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday between No. 21 UCLA vs. No. 13 Oregon . It doesn't sound like Dante Moore will suit up for the Ducks, but Oregon will look to add another ranked win to its resume. Here's how every Big Ten game could play out this weekend. MORE: College Football Big Ten power rankings entering Week 6 No. 7 Indiana vs. Nebraska NCAA Football: Indiana at Rutgers Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover (10) looks back after throwing a touchdown pass during the first half against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Indiana is doing what most people thought it would do. The Hoosiers don't have a blemish on the 2026 season , and quarterback Josh Hoover appears to have exorcised his interception woes that haunted him during his TCU years. Meanwhile, Nebraska is doing more than people thought. Despite losing quarterback Dylan Raiola to Oregon, the Huskers are 5-0 and have the No. 3 rushing attack of all Big Ten teams this season. Transfer Antony Colandrea is a good dual-threat quarterback, and freshman Jamal Rule has led the Nebraska rushing attack with 333 yards, despite being banged up. This game is in Lincoln and Nebraska will have to run the ball to win. But IU has the No. 1 rushing defense in the Big Ten, allowing fewer than 65 yards per game on the ground. This will be the first game Nebraska falls. Final score: Indiana 31, Nebraska 20 No. 21 UCLA vs. No. 13 Oregon Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, 2026, at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bob Chesney has really turned UCLA around in a hurry. The Bruins are one of the pleasant surprises in college football, and he has UCLA 4-0 with a major game this weekend. James Madison transfer Wayne Knight is second in the Big Ten, averaging over 111 yards on the ground. UCLA might have some good news. Quarterback Dante Moore won't play this weekend, which sets up backup Raiola to start. While facing the backup is a good thing, Raiola is no typical backup. He started the last two seasons at Nebraska, and came in against USC and played well. The Ducks are loaded with playmakers, and all Raiola has to do is run the offense. The Bruins are a feel-good story, but Oregon has turned a corner and will be tough to beat in Eugene. Final score: Oregon 38, UCLA 27 No. 19 USC vs. Penn State NCAA Football: Washington at Southern California USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) looks to pass the ball against the Washington Huskies during the second half at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Both of these teams are at a crossroads, but for different reasons. USC is supposed to be a College Football Playoff team in 2026, but a typical loss to Oregon has the Trojans on the brink. Another loss could push USC out of contention. As for Penn State, it had the most favorable schedule in the Big Ten, and head coach Matt Campbell had an outside chance to contend for a Big Ten title in Year 1. However, PSU has dropped the last two games against Wisconsin and Northwestern to move to 3-2 on the season. A .500 start is staring right at Penn State. When you look at these wo teams, there is a path for either to win, but USC is playing like the better team, and we've yet to see Penn State bounce back under its new staff. White Out or not, the Trojans get a big win. Final score: USC 30, Penn State 28 The rest of the games will be quick-hitter style: Washington 20, No. 20 Iowa 17 Northwestern 38, Ball State 7 Illinois 27, Michigan State 20 No. 5 Ohio State 41, Maryland 10 Minnesota 24, Purdue 17

Klatt's Week 6 CFB Picks Updated Oct. 8, 2026 11:34 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Headlining Week 6 of the college football season is a top-10 matchup in Georgia vs. Alabama, and the annual Red River Rivalry between Texas and Oklahoma. The Crimson Tide and the Bulldogs split last year when Alabama took down Georgia in the regular season, but the Bulldogs answered right back with an SEC title win over Bama. Texas remains atop the 2026 rankings with a comfortable 5-0 record that includes top-15 victories over Ohio State and Tennessee, and the Sooners look to hold off the Longhorns with a rebound win after a big loss to Georgia. Notably, UCLA and Bob Chesney will travel north to Eugene to face Oregon, where Chesney fell to the Ducks as JMU's head coach in the College Football Playoff last season. With a dominant run game and a shaky Oregon defense, the Bruins have a chance to hand the Ducks their second loss of the season. Here are FOX Sports' Joel Klatt's Week 6 picks and previews: Georgia 27, Alabama 24 Spread: Alabama 1.5 Moneyline: Alabama -122, Georgia +102 Klatt's thoughts: "This one is going to be an amazing game. Kirby Smart always has a great defense. They are great, once again. They have the No. 1 defense in the country as it relates to yards per play. They can get after it. They're going to have to get after it because Alabama's offense is explosive. Alabama can play offense, and Keelon Russell can throw the ball down the field. I think NFL evaluators should be salivating when he becomes available in the NFL Draft. He reminds me a lot of the way Michael Penix Jr. played at Washington for Kalen DeBoer, and yet he's more explosive and more mobile as a runner. So it's a deadly combination. "I think that Georgia has to put pressure on them. If they don't put pressure on Keelon Russell, I think Georgia loses the game. They've got to impact him somehow … it will be about the Georgia defense. I know the offense will be methodical. They will try to stay on schedule, they've got a quarterback who plays great in the fourth quarter … I think the worse the weather, the better for Kirby and Georgia. I don't know if Alabama can run the football without the impact of a great passing game. "I'm going to take Georgia … who I think is the best team in the country." Klatt's straight-up pick: Georgia Klatt's pick against the spread: Georgia +1.5 Texas 20, Oklahoma 10 Will Arch Manning succeed against Oklahoma's defense? (Photo by The University of Texas Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Spread: Texas -7.5 Moneyline: Texas -325, Oklahoma +260 Klatt's thoughts: "Texas and Oklahoma. Texas has won three of the last four meetings with Oklahoma. Texas is No. 1 in the country right now. They should be ranked No. 1. They are better on paper than they are on film. They've been wildly inconsistent as a team and specifically on the offensive side. I don't have a lot of worries about the Texas defense. The offense has not been very good … Penalties, not throwing the ball well, Arch has not played very well … they've got the best résumé, two top-15 wins. They've earned this position where they're at. Now they play a top-five defense in OU. "OU can play defense now. Their issue is definitely not their defense. In a lot of ways, these teams mirror each other. What if I told you Oklahoma is 112th in yards per play offense? They turned the ball over, they couldn't do anything against Michigan. What if I told you that Texas is 108th in yards per play offense? They're basically the same team … they've got great defenses and great offenses that are woefully underperforming. So what do I see in this game? I think it's low scoring. Just to give you some context, by the way … Texas is behind Colorado and Michigan in yards per play offense. When I tell you that they're better on paper than on film, it is the truth. "I think Texas wins, and covers, in a low-scoring affair 20-10, Texas and Arch Manning get the win at Red River." Klatt's straight-up pick: Texas Klatt's pick against the spread: Texas -7.5 Oregon 45, UCLA 32 The last time Bob Chesney was in Oregon, he was coaching JMU in the College Football Playoff. (Photo by CFP/Getty Images) Spread: Oregon -11.5 Moneyline: Oregon -455, UCLA +35 Klatt's thoughts: "Bob Chesney has UCLA undefeated right now. They're looking to pull off a huge upset in Eugene. Oregon is going to have to do a lot better at stopping the run than they have done during the course of the season. UCLA can absolutely run the football. They have one of the best run games in the country, averaging seven yards per rush. And they feature a guy in Wayne Knight that is explosive. Now here's the thing with UCLA: their quarterback can also run. He might not be the most dynamic runner, but Nico Iamaleava can absolutely threaten you in the run game. If I'm an Oregon fan, that makes me very nervous because of what Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker did, running that game in Stillwater. Wayne Knight is outstanding. "By the way, Bob Chesney took his JMU team to Eugene for the College Football Playoff, and yes, Oregon won handily, but guess what? JMU scored over 30 points … I think that [UCLA is] going to score some points here. Now the question will become, can Oregon match them and exceed them on the opposite side? I expect to see [Dylan] Raiola, he has bit of a penalty for turnovers, even though we didn't see that at USC when he came off the bench, but if you look back at his time with Nebraska, there are some turnovers there … I don't quite trust the UCLA defense. This is a defense that allowed 38 points to Purdue. "Oregon gets it done. I think Oregon wins 45-32, and they cover the 11.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Oregon Klatt's pick against the spread: Oregon -11.5 USC 32, Penn State 14 The Matt Campbell era is not off to a great start, and Joel Klatt doesn't think it's going to get better this week. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Spread: Penn State -1.5 Moneyline: Penn State -122, USC +105 Klatt's thoughts: "USC on the road, going east. USC, now 5-1, is at Penn State, who's now 3-2 and is unranked, and the bottom has kind of fallen out for Matt Campbell … What is going on? Penn State is favored by 1.5. [USC] just played awful football for six quarters. … The big question for me is, is USC going to beat themselves, or will they play a cleaner game? … When you just evaluate the teams and the product on the field, by 1.5 seems wild. USC is facing their old defensive coordinator, with a familiar piece there in D'Anton Lynn. I think the familiarity favors Lincoln Riley … USC should be able to run the ball. Penn State can't tackle anybody. The only one that gets in the way for USC, in my estimation, are the costly mistakes. Those might show up. I don't think USC's defense is great, but I think they're better than people give them credit for. "Penn State can't do anything on offense. They really miss their wide receiver, Koby Howard. He was averaging 100 yards per game on nearly 30 per catch. Since he went down, they've really struggled on offense. Rocco Becht has struggled on offense. They couldn't do anything against Northwestern. Couldn't do anything in the second half against Wisconsin. USC is better than Wisconsin and Northwestern talent wise. Klatt's straight-up pick: USC Klatt's pick against the spread: USC +1.5 LSU 28, Kentucky 10 Will Stein has Kentucky exceeding expectations in his first year at the helm, but LSU's defense looms. (Photo by Zach Del Bello/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -9.5 Moneyline: LSU -345, Kentucky +275 Klatt's thoughts: "LSU at Kentucky. LSU is favored by 9.5. Kentucky beat a very average Texas A&M and a very average-to-bad South Carolina team. They hung with Alabama for a half and then kind of got ran out of that building. I still am a bit concerned for LSU about the health of their quarterback. Sam Leavitt can't play the way that he normally plays ... his health is paramount for this team. Their defense is outstanding. This is where I think it really makes a huge difference in this game. Their defense is better than Alabama's defense. Kenny Minchey is going to see guys who can get after the passer. Princewill Umanmielen has eight sacks … Will Stein is doing awesome … he's exceeding expectations for Kentucky . But LSU is a different animal. This defense is a different animal. They can rush the passer and run everywhere. They're one of the best defenses in America. "I think Kentucky has to play their best. Do I anticipate them playing their best after the emotional win a week ago? No. History suggests that over the course of the season that very rarely can teams do something on the positive side, in an emotional fashion, and back it up with consistency the next week. So, I don't see Kentucky playing at the level they need to stay within the 9.5. "I got LSU winning this game 28-10. LSU covers the 9.5." away.blurb: UCLA starting safety Tao Johnson is questionable to play against Oregon. Starting UCLA safety Tao Johnson has missed the Bruins' last three games, and he's officially questionable to play Saturday against Oregon , according to the initial Big Ten availability report released Wednesday. Johnson is battling a shoulder injury and hasn't played since UCLA's season-opening win over Cal. Additionally, backup defensive lineman Ashton Sanders is listed as doubtful on the injury report. Other than Johnson, Sanders and Mikey Matthews , who's out for the rest of the season with a foot injury, every other player on the Bruins' two-deep is is currently cleared to play. For Oregon, starting quarterback Dante Moore , who suffered a concussion against USC in Week 4, won't play this week. That means Oregon backup and former Nebraska starting quarterback Dylan Raiola will get the start against the Bruins. Raiola completed 19-of-25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns in Oregon's win over USC after Moore got hurt. away.blurb: Of course, Dante Moore's designation as "out" was unsurprising, considering the concussion that he suffered just over a week ago against the USC Trojans . But the Ducks might also be without starting safety Aaron Flowers for Saturday's game as well. While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. As expected, Oregon starting quarterback Dante Moore has been listed as "out" ahead of Saturday's game against the UCLA Bruins. Following his concussion in the USC game, there was an assumption that Moore would miss at least one game, and potentially more. We will watch how he progresses over the next few days and monitor his status ahead of the Nebraska game in Week 7. According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Sitting at 4-1 overall, with just one bad half against Alabama against them, the Wildcats are on a three-game win streak that included a road win at then-No. 9 Texas A&M. (Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tina Howell Mon, October 5, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's Week 6, and the LSU Tigers will be on the road this Saturday night to take on Kentucky Wildcats. LSU will enter this SEC road matchup against Kentucky at 4-1 after cruising past McNeese 63-14 on Saturday night. The Tigers have now won two straight since their loss at Ole Miss, including an impressive 35-6 victory over Texas A&M. Kentucky also comes into this matchup at 4-1 after escaping South Carolina with a 35-34 overtime victory Saturday. The Wildcats have now won three straight since suffering their only loss of the season, a 45-17 defeat against Alabama. For LSU, the game represents an opportunity to build on the momentum of the past two weeks while picking up a much-needed SEC road victory. The Tigers have looked like a much more complete team since their loss at Ole Miss, particularly on defense, and will now have to carry that success away from Tiger Stadium. The Wildcats have already shown they can be dangerous in the SEC after going into College Station and defeating Texas A&M 31-21 before surviving an overtime battle at South Carolina. Now they will return home looking to add another victory to their record against LSU. Saturday will also mark LSU's first trip to Lexington since 2021, when Kentucky defeated the Tigers 42-21. LSU hasn't won at Kentucky since the memorable 33-30 "Bluegrass Miracle" in 2002, adding another storyline to the Tigers season. According to our friends at FanDuel, LSU is currently a 9.5-point favorite over Kentucky with the over/under set at 54.5 points. However, expect some movement in those numbers as the week progress. Kickoff is scheduled for 6:00p.m. CT at Kroger Field in Lexington on ESPN. Do you agree with the odds? picks.headline: ‘This one has a chance to stay pretty close for a really long time' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of LSU vs Kentucky
picks.blurb: ‘This one has a chance to stay pretty close for a really long time' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of LSU vs Kentucky - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers will travel to Lexington this weekend for a road matchup against the Kentucky Wildcats. The LSU Tigers will look to avoid a "letdown" this weekend in a road matchup against the Kentucky Wildcats. Saturday will mark the first matchup between the two programs since 2021 when Kentucky beat LSU 42-21 in Lexington. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of LSU vs Kentucky ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his predictions on Tuesday for this weekend's biggest games, and he has LSU just barely getting by Kentucky. "I'm taking the LSU Tigers to win the game 30-24," said McElroy . "I think they're going to win this game with the pass rush, and I do think there's going to be plenty of opportunities for LSU's defensive front to create some advantages behind the line of scrimmage. "But with (LSU QB) Sam Leavitt still a little bit limited right now, I think this one has a chance to stay pretty close for a really long time. Kentucky's comeback last week (against South Carolina) was historic, but against this pass rush, they can't afford to be playing from behind from start to finish." It's never easy to win on the road in the SEC. Kentucky isn't as daunting of a venue as some other places in the conference, but it can still be a challenge. LSU would love to win this game by multiple touchdowns, and maybe they do, but just simply getting the win is the top objective for the Tigers on Saturday night in Lexington. Despite erasing a 17-point deficit on the road against South Carolina last weekend to improve to 4-1, the Wildcats are walking into their first home night game of the Will Stein era as massive 9.5-point underdogs against LSU. The oddsmakers are essentially daring Big Blue Nation to bet on their own team, and I know some of you probably already did. LSU is definitely going to be one of the hardest tests of the season for Will Stein, Jay Bateman, and Joe Sloan. The Tigers bring an explosive offense and the No. 2 rushing defense in the country to Lexington. However, Kentucky loves turnovers, coming in 12th in the country right now. And LSU isn't a team that is particularly strong with the ball. Sam Leavitt has thrown seven interceptions, and the Tigers as a team have fumbled it six times so far this season, though they have been able to recover each of them. That will be a big key to this game, I think. If Kentucky can turn LSU over and capitalize with points, this should be a close game. If the Cats can't, then LSU's offense may be too much. picks.headline: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule
picks.blurb: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Story by Wildcats Wire LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:53 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football hosts a top ten team in the LSU Tigers under the lights of Kroger Field, and the bluegrass is as fired up as ever coming off the largest comeback road win in program history. The energy is at an all time high in Lexington, as Will Stein has kicked off his first year as head coach with a 4-1 record. Kentucky was dropped out of the AP top 25 after their road win at South Carolina, this will add some motivation as this is just the third time since 2000 a team was dropped from the top 25 following a win. We previewed Lane Kiffin's dynamic offense he is bringing with him, now it is time to preview the Tigers defense that is statistically one of the best in the conference. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker was retained by Kiffin as he has done a phenomenal job with the Tigers defense. This is a defense loaded with talent, but will unfortunately be without the leader and green dot in Whit Weeks. LSU gave up 32 points on the road at Ole Miss, they have allowed just 44 total points in their other four games combined. That game was big for a lot of reasons, but when you look at the statistics per secstatcat.com; Kentucky and Ole Miss have very similar numbers offensively. Kentucky - SEC Rank Ole Miss - SEC Rank Early Down Conv. % Ole Miss, similar to Kentucky, has also struggled on converting 3rd downs this season. Ole Miss has definitely been better on third downs, but is still an area they need to improve on. Both Kentucky and Ole Miss have canceled out their third down woes by converting on early downs. They are first and second in the SEC in converting on early downs, and they join Georgia and Alabama as the only SEC teams that are converting over 50% on early downs. This is an area Kentucky has to continue to have success in to win this game, staying on schedule is a huge factor in this football game. Kentucky cannot get in 3rd and long as that is when LSU can overwhelm you with the talent they have on the defensive line. Princewill Umanmielen followed Kiffin over from Ole Miss and he is a true game wrecker off the edge. Umanmielen leads all of college football with eight sacks on the season, this will be a true test for both tackles Lance Heard and Malachi Wood. Another interesting aspect of this matchup is the relationship of Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker. They worked together for years at Louisiana Tech and obviously spent the last couple of season together at LSU. They know each other really well, and they could know tendencies of each other as play callers that could create advantages in certain situations. Sloan knows a good amount of the roster at LSU, and it is intriguing to see if that can pose advantages for the Wildcats. The LSU defense has been incredible against the pass game, as they lead the SEC in EPA/dropback allowed. Their secondary is led by corner DJ Pickett and safety Ty Benefield, both players are NFL Draft prospects that can make plays at every level of the field. Their starting slot corner Dashawn Spears tore his ACL and is out for the season. This has led Ty Benefield to playing that spot in nickel formations, and he will have his hands full with Louisiana native, breakout true freshman slot receiver Kenny Darby This will be an extra special game for a lot of people on Kentucky's offense. Offensive coordinator Joe Sloan was fired as offensive coordinator at LSU before making the move to Lexington. Kenny Darby broke high school receiving records in the state of Louisiana and was committed to LSU for a long time. Wide receiver Nic Anderson also transferred over from LSU. Kentucky's offense will continue to be difficult for opposing defenses, as the scheme just constantly forces you to communicate. This LSU defense has a ton of playmakers, but Kentucky can find success as long as they stay on schedule. Kentucky is one of the best offenses in creating yards before contact and the offensive line has been steady in pass protection all season. The Wildcats offensive line has to find a way to win the line of scrimmage in this game, and it is easier said than done with this stout LSU defensive line. Kentucky will have to find success on offense to win this football game. Expect Lane Kiffin and Charlie Weis to put points on the board as they always do. This is a defense similar to Alabama, where Kentucky struggled to consistently move the football on in week two. There is no doubt the Wildcats offense has improved since then, but we will see just how much they have improved on Saturday. away.headline: LSU football injury report | Who made the list ahead of Kentucky game?
away.blurb: News Sports Business Living Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals LSU LSU football injury report | Who made the list ahead of Kentucky game? Cory Diaz Lafayette Daily Advertiser Updated Oct. 7, 2026, 7:29 p.m. CT BATON ROUGE — LSU football' s initial injury report for this weekend's game at Kentucky is out. For the first time this season, there are no surprises on the report for Lane Kiffin and the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 SEC). LSU does not have any players listed as probable, questionable or doubtful on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 7 by the SEC. Weeks and Green have not been ruled out for the rest of the season but have suffered leg injuries that will keep them out for a substantial amount of time. The No. 10-ranked Tigers face No. 25 Kentucky (4-1, 1-1) inside Kroger Field on Saturday, Oct. 10 (6 p.m. CT, ESPN). As expected, star linebacker Whit Weeks, tight end Trey'Dez Green , safety Dashawn Spears, as well as reserves and special teams players Charles Ross II and receiver Phillip Wright Jr., are on the list. Spears, Ross and Wright have suffered season-ending injuries. Weeks fractured his fibula against Texas A&M on Sept. 26 and has had a successful surgery to correct it. Green sprained his knee in the Ole Miss game and has missed the past two games for LSU. But earlier this week, Kiffin said the tight end was getting closer to playing. away.blurb: The LSU Tigers return to SEC play this weekend against the Kentucky Wildcats, which means another week of official injury reports to prepare for the week. Here are the initial reports put out by the conference : No news is good news for LSU. They have five players ruled out, but all were expected to be out. There was nothing unexpected here. It is good to see the cornerback depth improving, with Ja'Keem Jackson off the report entirely. It is a long list for Kentucky this week, but nothing completely detrimental. They do have five players already listed out, the same as the Tigers, but only one was a Week 1 starter. Their depth has been completely wiped out, which could always come into play as well. Patterson has been a key piece of their offense and left the game early against the South Carolina Gamecocks, so he was uncertain for this one. It looks like he'll be fully healthy. Gates is a high-potential player who has dealt with injuries that have hampered him throughout most of his career. He missed last week, but is their starting slot corner when healthy. That's an important role against this Lane Kiffin offense. Edwards is one to watch as he has been a large part of the defensive interior rotation and did pick up half a sack against the Alabama Crimson Tide . Miller coming back could be big. He was a four-star in last year's class, had a breakout game as a freshman, but wasn't a consistent part of the offense. He had zero catches through two weeks, but had five catches for 96 yards against the Texas A&M Aggies .

home.headline: Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable'
home.blurb: The Bears (2-3, 1-1 ACC) return home Saturday to face Virginia Tech (3-2, 1-1) in a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Memorial Stadium. Will JKS miss his first game in two seasons or could he return to face the Hokies? We don’t know. Turns out Sagapolutele continued to show “some symptoms” during the second half and he now is among four Cal players undergoing multiple tests every day as part of the Bears’ concussion protocol program. Safety Kingston Lopa is also facing those protocols, Lupoi said. Besides Lopa going out with the head injury, the Bears played portions of the UNLV game without defensive backs Cam Sidney and Daniel Harris, both ejected after targeting penalties. Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable' Skip to main content SI.COM Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is among 10 Cal starters dealing with injuries — one of four in concussion protocol — coach Tosh Lupoi reported Tuesday. Cal is not required to provide details about injuries, although we will get status updates when the ACC releases its initial player availability chart on Wednesday night. We do know this much: Cal football athletic director and general manager Ron Rivera was not happy with the play that led to Sagapolutele leaving the game in the final minute of the half at UNLV. Rivera called the injury “avoidable.” Cal was trailing 24-7 when JKS rolled right and threw incomplete on first-and-10 from his own 25-yard line. UNLV linebacker Elias Rudolph, a transfer from Miami, flung Sagapolute to the artificial turf and the sophomore QB’s head bounced off the artificial turf. No flag was thrown, but Rivera clearly believed that should have happened. “JKS’s concussion, in my opinion, was avoidable. And I agree with Tosh, something should have happened,” he said. “When the quarterback throws the ball and the defender sees him throw the ball, there’s no reason to allow him to violently grab a guy and swirl around him and throw him to the ground. "Just go back and watch the tape. That’s all I’m going to say about that.” Lupoi removed Sagapolutele from the game after watching him stagger back to the huddle. At halftime, he was told JKS was cleared to play, but Lupoi said he didn’t feel comfortable sending him back onto the field. With backup Jackson Brousseau performing well at quarterback, Cal rallied to take a 25-24 lead in the second half before the Rebels answered to win 39-31. The closest Lupoi came to providing a hint as to whether Sagapolutele might face Virginia Tech was when he offered, “He was cleared to go back in at one point. That tells you it was a minor whatever-you-want-to-call-it.” Cal already has been playing without injured running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas. The Bears were desperate enough at the position that wide receivers Tyree Sams and Carson Perry-Smith were given snaps — and carries — at running back in Saturday. “You may or may not see that this week,” Lupoi said. home.headline: Cal Football Game Summary: Bears Lose to UNLV; Sagapolutele Injured
home.source: California Golden Bears On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. Although he passed for just 158 yards, he threw touchdown passes of 70, 36 and 10 yards and ran for a 55-yard touchdown. He also had a key 42-yard run and finished with 110 rushing yards. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. KEY PLAY 2: Cal safety Kingston Lopa, who leads the nation in interceptions with five, left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter. KEY PLAY 3: Sagapolutele completed a 91-yard touchdown pass to freshman tight end Taimane Purcell, who covered most of the ground himself. It gave Cal a 7-0 lead with 11:30 remaining in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 4 : Cal starting safety Cam Sidney was ejected for targeting with 11:25 left in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 5: On a third-and-8 play from the UNLV 30-yard line, Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold completed a 70-yard touchdown
