Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect C B Mon, October 5, 2026 at 12:59 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Right about now, there are college football writers across the nation who are absolutely seething. Steam is coming out of their ears. They are irate because the Alabama dynasty is not dead and they actually have to write good things about the Crimson Tide. Alabama (5-0) has run roughshod over their competition. The Tide has averaged 49.6 point per game and no game has been below 45 points in scoring for Bama. The Bulldogs have had a simpler schedule but have had similar results. UGA has averaged 51.4 ppg but the last two games have been 41 and 38 points scored. In short, these two teams score a good deal of points. In the preseason, Georgia was a FanDuel +2.5 favorite over Alabama. But much has changed and the the script has flipped. FanDuel now has opening odds of Alabama being a 1.5 point favorite over the Bulldogs with an Over/Under of 55.5 . So far this season, the sportsbooks have pegged UGA with healthy point spreads as well as decent sized Over/Under in each game. However ,most of them have been too low. Sept 5 vs Tennessee State: -49.5 / 55.5, Won 63-3 (-60, 66), Won / Over Sept 12 Western Kentucky: -40.5 / 55.5 Won, 70-20 (-50, 90), Won/ Over Sept 19 @Arkansas: -24.5 / 54.5, Won 45-17 (-28, 62), Won/ Over Sep 26 vs Oklahoma: -11.5 / 43.5, Won 41-13 (-28, 54), Won / Over Oct 3 vs Vanderbilt: -25.5 / 49.5, Won 38-14 (-24, 52), Lost / Over The Dwags have not really had any close games. Much like Alabama, the Vegas bookies have been giving UGA some pretty low numbers. They covered the spread and went over the points total in each of their first four games. This past weekend was the first bucking of that trend as the Doggies did not cover and had their lowest points total of the young season. In preseason, many observers figured Oklahoma would be a tougher competition. But who knew John Mateer would be such dog poo and gift the Bulldogs so many points? It is a mystery why anyone thinks a post-Diego Pavia Vanderbilt would be anything worth worrying about. Arkansas is in a deep funk. All that said, Georgia really has not played anyone worth a hill o' beans. To date, UGA opponents are collectively 9-15. Their Strength of Schedule is 97th. Alabama foes are 15-9. The Tide SOS is 23rd. The Las Vegas guys have underestimated the Tide all season. The Bama Boys have been killing the Over/Unders and had only one misstep against the spread. Sep 5 vs East Carolina: -28.5/52.5, Won 48-10 (-38, 58), Won/Over Sep 12 at Kentucky: -9.5/47.5, Won 45-17 (-28, 62), Won/Over Sep 19, vs Florida State: -18.5 / 50.5, Won 50-36 (-14, 86), Lost / Over Sep 26 vs South Carolina: -12.5 / 53.5, Won 49-18 (-31, 67), Won / Over Oct 3, at Mississippi State: -5.5 / 63.5, Won 56-23 (-33, 59), Won / Over The Crimson Tide did not cover against Florida State but easily did so in the other four games. It was mentioned in this space last weak that perhaps the FSU game was a fluke. Upon further reflection, it might just be the rapid pace that Bama QB Keelon Russell is developing and improving. The Tide offense is stacking up some points. Georgia and Alabama are No. 1 and 3 respectively in scoring in FBS thus far this season. The Bulldogs are putting up 51.4 ppg but that number is skewed by the 70-burger they put up on woeful WKU (1-4) who yielded 49 to Nevada. This Bama-UGA game will be the game of the week under a lot of spotlights. It will be the secondAlabama night game following the South Carolina match-up. Early forecasts are calling for rain in Tuscaloosa on Saturday. But that is what they were saying about the MSU game as well. With an over/under of 55.5 and 1.5 point spread by FanDuel , the final score could look something like Bama 29-27 or so. Does that seem logical? Once again, I am going over on both of these lines. Both defenses for these teams are better than either has faced, but it just feels like both teams will go over 30 points with the Tide winning by 5 or so. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in Comments below.

picks.headline: Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown
picks.blurb: Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers return to NLCS Rays sweep Yankees Brewers clinch NLCS Valkyries, Dream win Game 2s NFL Power Rankings Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown (Petre Thomas-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:15 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The stage is set for the Alabama Crimson Tide to take on the Georgia Bulldogs this weekend in a massive SEC showdown. Alabama will be hosting the Bulldogs in the game, offering them a slight advantage coming into the contest. But this game will be anything but a bloodbath, with both sides desperately wanting to win. Each team enters this matchup with a record of 5-0, going 3-0 in SEC play so far this season. The two rivals have continuously given fans epic games over the years, and this matchup should be no different. Alabama comes in ranked No. 6 in the country, while Georgia is No. 2. For the Crimson Tide, they have a chance to take down one of the top teams in the nation at home, helping their own resume in the process. Entering the game, the matchup looks pretty even, with both teams having a real chance to take home the win. But according to ESPN's game predictor , Alabama has a slightly bigger opportunity to get the victory. Alabama has been given a 52.6 percent chance to take down Georgia, showing some of the slimmest of margins coming into the game. Part of why the Crimson Tide may be favored here is because the game is being played in Tuscaloosa. The Crimson Tide are very tough to beat at home, but Georgia is one of the few teams that has the talent to make it happen. Alabama will need to make sure that they bring their A-game into this matchup; otherwise, it could be a long night for everyone involved. Quarterback Keelon Russell is going to be tested in ways that he hasn't been so far this season, and he will need to prove that he can step up for the team. For Alabama to reach its big goals of winning a title this year, Russell is going to have to take on teams like Georgia while performing at a high level. But so far this year, Russell has passed all his tests with flying colors, entering his name into the Heisman Trophy conversation . If Russell can have another strong game against the Bulldogs, Alabama would likely be put in a good spot to grab the win at home. This is a measuring stick game for both teams, and the winner will have the upper hand to get into the College Football Playoff . Kickoff for this game will take place at 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from Bryant-Denny Stadium.

picks.headline: Josh Pate drops head-turning college football ‘Game of the Year’ prediction for Georgia-Alabama blockbuster

The Bulldogs haven't been tested much yet so far this year, but that's likely to change on Saturday against an explosive Crimson Tide offensive attack. Recently, college football media personality Josh Pate dropped a hot take in anticipation of the big matchup. "It's game of the year potential. It's not the end of the world for the loser. Both teams saw their respective seasons come to an unceremonious end in the quarterfinal round of the college football playoff. It will certainly be interesting to see how the Bulldogs respond if they find themselves in a close game against Alabama on Saturday, as Georgia has yet to find themselves up against any real adversity so far this season. One of the biggest features of GameDay is the "celebrity guest picker," which is usually a celebrity or athlete with ties to the university hosting GameDay. This season's guest pickers have featured the likes of Morgan Freeman and Lainey Wilson. While it is anyone's guess, here are five options for the GameDay guest picker in Tuscaloosa this Saturday. Young also has history with Georgia, having played against the Bulldogs in the 2021 SEC Championship Game in which he threw for 421 yards, as well as the 2021 CFP national championship. The Panthers have their bye week this upcoming weekend, which opens up the door schedule-wise for Young to potentially be the guest picker. Femi was a shot-put thrower at Alabama from 2019-22 where he was a two-time SEC Indoor conference champion. Femi toured the Alabama football facilities prior to the season, and was also featured on the "Paul Finebaum Show" at that time. Having one of the premier players of the last couple decades would be a smart decision for GameDay. Jones also has history with Georgia as he went for five catches, 94 yards, and a touchdown in Alabama's 41-30 win over Georgia in the infamous Georgia blackout game in Athens during his freshman season in 2008. Jones is also set to feature in the Nick Saban documentary that ESPN is putting out, of which the first episode of is set to be released on Thursday . Justin Thomas, pro golfer Sep 27, 2026; Medinah, Illinois, USA; Justin Thomas of the U.S. Team watches his birdie putt on the 15th green after putting to win his match during the final round of the Presidents Cup. Mandatory Credit: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images If GameDay elects to go back to someone who has been the guest picker before, professional golfer Justin Thomas could be the choice. No. 2 Georgia travels to Tuscaloosa Saturday night to face No. 6 Alabama in a 7:30 p.m. kickoff at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Both teams enter 5-0 and 3-0 in SEC play, making this one of the biggest games of the college football season. Georgia absolutely has a path to winning this game. The Bulldogs have the more experienced quarterback in Gunner Stockton, an elite rushing attack and a defense allowing just 13.4 points per game. Stockton has completed 75.5% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and only one interception. But there is one major concern: Can Georgia's defense get enough stops? Keelon Russell has been on fire. He has thrown for 1,414 yards with 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions while adding another four touchdowns on the ground. Alabama just went into Starkville and dropped 56 points on Mississippi State, with Russell throwing for 285 yards and three touchdowns. Georgia's defense has been good statistically, but it hasn't faced anything quite like this Alabama offense. The Bulldogs showed some cracks against Vanderbilt, allowing 293 yards and struggling to consistently get off the field on third down before tightening things up in the second half. Against Russell, those mistakes could become touchdowns. Georgia's best chance is to run the football, control possession and keep Russell standing on the Alabama sideline. Nate Frazier and the Bulldogs' offensive line can absolutely have success, and Stockton's efficiency gives Georgia another way to move the football if Alabama loads the box. The problem is that Alabama can counter by bringing pressure and trusting its secondary. Kirby Smart called Alabama's defensive backs talented, physical "ball hawks" and specifically pointed to the pressure created by the Crimson Tide's front. And then there is Bryant-Denny Stadium . This game being in Tuscaloosa matters. Georgia will be dealing with one of the loudest environments in college football against an Alabama team playing with a ton of confidence. Even the betting market has shifted toward the Crimson Tide, with Alabama currently sitting around a 1.5-point favorite after Georgia initially opened as the favorite. Prediction: Alabama 38, Georgia 27 I trust Georgia to move the football. I trust Stockton's experience, and I think the Bulldogs can establish the run. I just don't trust Georgia to get enough stops. Russell's ability to create outside structure is the difference. Georgia can defend the play perfectly and still watch Russell escape the pocket and turn it into an explosive gain. Add the home-field advantage, Alabama's veteran secondary and the Tide's ability to pressure Stockton, and the matchup starts leaning toward Bama. Georgia hangs around, but eventually Russell makes too many plays. Alabama 38, Georgia 27. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide

Will Keelon Russell continue his efficient freshman season against No. 6 Alabama's rival, No. 2 Georgia? In the Big Ten, Bob Chesney and No. 21 UCLA will try to stay undefeated as they travel to No. 13 Oregon. Matt Rhule will try to earn his first win against a ranked team when Nebraska plays No. 7 Indiana on "Big Noon Kickoff." Week 6 of the college football season features two historic rivalries with College Football Playoff implications, and more. We’re breaking down our straight-up picks and the matchups to watch closely throughout the weekend. Michael Cohen Washington vs. No. 20 Iowa Kirk Ferentz fell to 2-12 against Ohio State since becoming Iowa's head coach in 1999. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) When: Friday, 9:00 p.m. ET (FOX) Where: Husky Stadium, Seattle, Washington Line: Washington -3 RJ Young: Iowa I know what to expect from Iowa's offense and defense. I also know that unless Demond Williams Jr. is having a Kyler Murray day rather than a Jackson Arnold one, Washington is cooked. Laken Litman: Iowa The Hawkeyes rebound from a big loss to Ohio State with a decisive road win over the Huskies to keep them in the Big Ten title race. Michael Cohen: Iowa Back-to-back losses for Washington have left the Huskies teetering, and the Hawkeyes are more than capable of grinding out another impressive road win. Ben Portnoy: Iowa Washington has basically been Demond Williams Jr. and everyone else so far. Iowa got handled relatively routinely by Ohio State last week, but the Hawkeyes are far and away the better team in this matchup. Nebraska vs. No. 7 Indiana Curt Cignetti and the Indiana Hoosiers hold a 21-game winning streak, dating back to the 2024 College Football Playoff. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX) Where: Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, Nebraska Line: Indiana -7.5 Young: Indiana While it won't be the 56-7 beatdown it was last year, I expect the Hoosiers to handle Nebraska in Lincoln with little-to-no trouble. Litman: Indiana In what could be viewed as a look-ahead game before hosting Ohio State next week, coach Curt Cignetti ensures Indiana escapes Lincoln with another win. Cohen: Indiana There are levels to coaching, and Curt Cignetti is more than a cut above Matt Rhule. Leaning on defense, the Hoosiers should win comfortably. Portnoy: Indiana The last time Indiana and Nebraska played in a pseudo-prove-it game in 2024, the Hoosiers won 56-7. It won't be that lopsided, but Curt Cignetti and co. win on the road in Lincoln. No. 14 Missouri vs. Texas A&M Austin Simmons threw for a season-high 340 yards and two touchdowns in Missouri's win over Florida last Saturday. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) When: Saturday, noon ET (ABC) Where: Memorial Stadium, Columbia, Missouri Line: Missouri -3.5 Young: Missouri Quarterback Austin Simmons is coming off a 300-yard passing performance against a Florida defense that we thought was good. Texas A&M's defense, we know, is not. Litman: Missouri Two weeks ago, everyone was down on Mizzou after a loss to Mississippi State, but that decisive win over Florida has the Tigers back with momentum. It will continue against the struggling Aggies. Cohen: Missouri Quarterback Austin Simmons has now thrown 13 touchdowns without an interception for Missouri. He should be able to handle a Texas A&M defense ranked outside the top 40 nationally. Portnoy: Missouri Missouri shocked me and just about everyone else with its throttling of Florida last week. Austin Simmons is the best QB in the country no one is talking about. Give me the Tigers over a reeling Aggies squad. No. 21 UCLA vs. No. 13 Oregon Dan Lanning (Left) and Bob Chesney (Right) met when Oregon and James Madison faced off in the 2025 CFP. Chesney is now UCLA's head coach. (Photo by CFP/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (CBS) Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, Oregon Line: Oregon -11.5 Young: Oregon Dan Lanning might think UCLA reminds him of Indiana, and that might be enough to wake his team up as the Hoosiers are the last team to come into Autzen and walk out with a win. Unfortunately, UCLA doesn't have the quarterback play this season that Indiana had last season. Litman: Oregon UCLA is flying high under new coach Bob Chesney, but this game is at Autzen and the Ducks — whether they're led by quarterback Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola — seem to be heading in the right direction after a massive win over USC. Cohen: Oregon If this game was being played in Los Angeles, it would be quite tempting to take UCLA. But Autzen Stadium is a tough environment for a UCLA team that might be overachieving right now. Portnoy: Oregon I know we all kind of left Oregon for dead after Oklahoma State, but after the USC win and a bye week, I think Dan Lanning will get things rolling again. UCLA has taken massive strides under Bob Chesney. This just may be too tall of a task this early. Oklahoma vs. No. 1 Texas Texas has won three of the last four Red River Rivalry games against Oklahoma. (Photo by The University of Texas Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: Cotton Bowl, Dallas, Texas Line: Texas -8.5 Young: Texas Name the number, Longhorns. Oklahoma is a terrible offensive team. Litman: Texas You never really know with a rivalry game, but Texas has never lost to Oklahoma when ranked No. 1 in the country and that trend won't change now. Cohen: Texas Not much to overthink in this one. Yes, it's a rivalry game, but the Longhorns might be the most complete team in the country. A lopsided win. Portnoy: Texas Red River has a tendency to get weird, but Oklahoma might be the worst team in the SEC outside of Arkansas. Give me the Longhorns, huge. Kansas State vs. No. 22 Houston Houston quarterback Conner Weigman rushed for 50 yards and three touchdowns in the Cougars' win over UCF last Saturday. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FOX) Where: Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan, Kansas Line: KSU -2.5 Young: Houston Houston is one-inch from being undefeated and one of the favorites to win the Big 12 title. Litman: Houston Conner Weigman may not have passed for a TD last week, but he ran for three scores, and he'll probably use his legs again against Kansas State's lowly run defense. Cohen: Houston The only loss for the Cougars this season came on the road against a team now ranked No. 11 nationally in Texas Tech. Houston can take down K-State on the road. Portnoy: Kansas State The Wildcats have flown under the radar a touch in Collin Klein's first year, but they might just have unlocked what we've been hoping for out of Avery Johnson for years. I like Kansas State in a mild upset. UNLV vs. North Dakota State Tim Polasek and North Dakota State have jumped out to a 5-0 record in their first FBS season. (Photo by Scott Marshall/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:00 p.m. ET (CW) Where: Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas, Nevada Line: NDSU -3 Young: North Dakota State The Bison are the only team in the country I expect to finish 12-0. Litman: North Dakota State First-year FBS team North Dakota State continues its march toward a potential Group of Six CFP berth with an impressive road win over coach Dan Mullen and UNLV. Cohen: North Dakota State Credit the Rebels for bouncing back from a blowout loss to North Texas with back-to-back victories, including one against an ACC opponent. But there's a reason big-time programs almost never want to play NDSU. And UNLV is about to find out why. Portnoy: North Dakota State Nobody just waltzes into the Fargodome and leaves with a win. Dan Mullen may be angling for his next SEC head coaching job (Hello, South Carolina), but the Bison have been uber-impressive in their first season in FBS. I like the home team here. Litman: LSU While Will Stein has been a home run hire for Kentucky, Lane Kiffin's LSU is the more talented team and has the nation's No. 2 defense. Cohen: LSU Even though quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown at least one interception in every game this season, the Tigers should handle Kentucky thanks to the No. 2 defense in the country. Portnoy: LSU Kentucky was lucky to leave South Carolina with a win last week, but I like what I've seen from Kenny Minchey. Still, I'm rolling with LSU's overall talent and this gives Lane Kiffin a nice win to get things rolling again post-Ole Miss. Penn State vs. No. 19 USC Lane Kiffin and USC bounced back to beat Washington in Week 5. (Photo by Ronaldo Bolaños/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC) Where: Beaver Stadium, University Park, Pennsylvania Line: Penn State -1.5 Young: USC Penn State has found its level, and USC can't afford to drop a game to an unranked opponent. Litman: USC Lincoln Riley is safe for another week, while Penn State — which gave up more than 400 yards rushing to Northwestern last week — loses its third game in a row. Cohen: USC Already regretting this choice given Lincoln Riley's propensity to struggle in difficult environments. But Penn State has looked downright dreadful in back-to-back losses. There's no good option here. Portnoy: Penn State Is this the end of the Lincoln Riley era? Perhaps. It's been an angsty week in State College as fans have revolted against administration in the wake of the Northwestern loss. I'll take Matt Campbell to get a win in his first White Out game. No. 6 Alabama vs. No. 2 Georgia Kalen DeBoer holds a 2-1 record against Georgia as Alabama's head coach. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC) Where: Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa, Alabama Line: Alabama -1.5 Young: Georgia Alabama's shot-play offense against UGA's suffocating defense? I'll take the Dawgs. Litman: Georgia Sure, Georgia hasn't been challenged yet this year, but in primetime, the Bulldogs show they're for real and overcome a good performance by Alabama's Heisman-contending quarterback, Keelon Russell. Cohen: Georgia If Texas isn't the most complete team in the country, then Georgia probably is. The Bulldogs lead the country in scoring offense and rank seventh in total defense. That's too much for the Crimson Tide to handle. Portnoy: Alabama I was incredibly skeptical of the Alabama defense early this season, but that may just simply not matter the way the Tide are scoring points. Keelon Russell has the first of what could be a few Heisman moments and Kalen DeBoer wins another huge game as Alabama head coach. Fresno State vs. No. 23 Boise State Boise State running back Dylan Riley (0) leads the Pac-12 in rushing yards in 2026. (Sarah A. Miller/Idaho Statesman/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) When: Saturday, 10:30 p.m. ET (CW) Where: Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno, California Line: Boise State -6.5 Young: Boise State Fresno State has done little this season to show me its capable of such an upset. Litman: Boise State The Broncos keep their winning streak alive and CFP hopes intact with a quality road win over a 4-1 Fresno State team. Cohen: Boise State As ever, the Broncos remain legitimate contenders

Alabama right tackle Jayvin James is not featured on the initial availability report. James left the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early with a lower extremity injury, and it forced him to sit out of the Mississippi State victory. Alabama tight end Josh Ford broke his arm during the Mississippi State. DeBoer said during Wednesday's teleconference that even though Ford received arm surgery this past Sunday, DeBoer is optimistic about him playing against Georgia. "Actually, progressing along fairly well right now," DeBoer said . "We'll kind of see how the week continues for him, and I know where his mindset's at. Penn State was blown out by Northwestern last week, with the team performing poorly on both sides of the ball. After three straight wins to open the year, the Nittany Lions are now back to the drawing board for ways to right the ship. Head coach Matt Campbell will have to get his guys back on track, and the schedule-makers didn't do them any favors this week. Penn State will be hosting the USC Trojans this weekend, giving the team a chance to take on a top-20 opponent. This matchup will test the Nittany Lions, seeing how they can perform against one of the top teams in the country. Penn State will try to pull off the upset, and if they can, the last few weeks will be more of a blip on the season. Coming into the game, Penn State is being favored to win, at least by ESPN's game predictor . The Nittany Lions have been given a 62 percent chance to upset the Trojans, earning a massive win at home. Penn State may be favored in the game due to the game being played at home, with the Nittany Lions having a strong home-field advantage. But this team does have talent, and despite the two losses in a row, this matchup gives them an opportunity to showcase it. Quarterback Rocco Becht will be the key in this game, and he is going to need to put together a better performance this week. Becht has struggled in each of the past two games, leading to the losses for the Nittany Lions. While the struggles from Penn State aren't all on his shoulders, Becht does make a big difference to this team. For the season, the veteran signal-caller has thrown for 1,108 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Against an opportunistic Trojans defense, Becht will need to limit his turnovers, keeping the ball with the offense. USC has a strong offensive-attack, and if they are given more opportunities or shirt fields, it may be a tough game for Penn State. Penn State has the means to pull off an upset win against the Trojans in this game, and if they can, they could build momentum for the rest of the season. Kickoff between the Nittany Lions and Trojans is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET.

PENN STATE: 0-1 Tony Rojas is the only active player with more than 21 career TFLs and six career interceptions…Saturday will be the 19th full stadium white out in Beaver Stadium history…USC and Penn State are both in the top 10 in program wins and winning percentage…USC leads the all-time series 6-5 over Penn State…the two programs will be meeting for the second time as members of the Big Ten. Jayden Maiava is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation when he heats up. The likely future first round draft pick has continually improved in three years as a starter, and is enjoying his best season up to this point. He is completing 69% of his passes with 15 touchdowns and three interceptions, and is on pace to set career highs in just about every category. Maiava has accomplished this without wide receiver Trent Mosely, who was quickly establishing himself as one of the nation's best receivers as a true freshman. He has been out with an injury since week two, and is not likely to return on Saturday. The Trojans still have their typical number of playmakers at the skill positions. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, a freshman with the body of a veteran NFL receiver, has become the primary targets with 25 catches for 372 yards and three scores. Zacharyus Williams, another big-bodied receiver, has been a dangerous deep threat and is coming off his best game. Maiva also looks to tight end Mark Bowman often, a freshman who has become more involved with the offense in recent weeks – although he is questionable with an undisclosed injury. King Miller returns to the USC offense after rushing for just under 1,000 yards as a true freshman. He came back bigger and faster, and can be hard to take down at 6-0, 225 lbs. He can also be dangerous in the open field despite his size, and has a run of at least 20 yards in each of the past four games. Waymond Jones is another big, physical back who excels in short yardage situations. Penn State's defense appeared to be the strength of the team, and one of the best in the Big Ten. However, that sentiment was erased by Northwestern on Friday in of the poorest defensive performances in recent memory. The Wildcats put up 406 rushing yards, averaging 7.5 yards with each carry. Northwestern was able to run so freely that they only had 14 passing attempts while controlling the clock. It doesn't help that they will be facing a coach in Lincoln Riley that excels at creating offensive gameplans, and was just handed a blueprint for how to move the ball on the defense. It's hard to find any current point of optimism for the Penn State offense. The tackles have been unable to set the edge. The interior line is unable to open up running lanes or keep the pocket clean. The running backs have failed to find explosive plays, or provide a consistent ground game. Tight end Andrew Rapplyea and center Brock Riker are both playing through injuries that are obviously limiting their play. The receivers have shown promise, but don't get many chances because of all the off-target passes and balls regularly getting knocked down at the line of scrimmage. Rocco Becht has not yet shown he is capable of moving the ball against a Big Ten defense through two games. Despite being the nation's most experienced quarterback, he has often looked lost within the offense once the level of competition improved. Fortunately for Penn State, they are facing a defense that has been struggling after a positive start in non-conference play. The Trojans are ranked 14th or worse in the Big Ten in scoring defense, pass defense, total defense, and explosive plays allowed. USC gave up 30 points against Louisiana, 35 against Rutgers and 41 to Oregon in consecutive weeks. They are coming off a better result against a Washington offense decimated by injuries, holding them to 21 points and a key stop in the final minute to preserve the victory over the Huskies. If Penn State can find some rhythm, it may be against this defense. Safety Christian Pike is USC's most productive player, and should be on an NFL roster next season. He leads the team with 35 tackles, and has an interception and two pass breakups. Similar to Penn State, USC has a pass rush by committee and do not seem to have a dominate pass rusher who regularly makes plays in the backfield. Penn State fans will also recognize a couple of former Nittany Lions who transferred to USC over the off-season in linebacker Ta'Mere Robinson and defensive end Zuriah Fisher. SPECIAL TEAMS USC kicker Caden Chittenden is 6-of-7 on the season, with a career-long of 52 yards in 2024 while playing at UNLV. Punter Lachlan Carrigan is as consistent as they come, and has an average of 49.3 yards per punt. Penn State kicker Ryan Barker missed his second field goal of the season on Friday after not missing a single field goal that was not blocked in 2025. Barker has a career high of 49 yards, which he has hit on multiple occasions. Punter Nathan Tiyce is averaging 41.6 yards per punt this season, and is coming off a shaky performance against Northwestern with several short kicks. USC-27, Penn State-17 Maybe Penn State is able to prove they are better than the team we've watched in the last two weeks. Maybe there are some quick fixes to set things right. But for now, it appears the Nittany Lions are lost and searching for answers that may never come. It could be this team just isn't good enough to beat a quality opponent. Penn State will likely come out fighting and be boosted by the White Out crowd. However, my prediction comes to one simple fact – USC's offense can move the ball. Penn State still hasn't proven they can do so.

Penn State lost to Wisconsin (24-20) and Northwestern (34-13) allowing the most points of the season back-to-back weeks. Rocco Becht also threw interceptions back-to-back weeks and his first multi-interception game at Northwestern. The Nittany Lions are in danger of falling to .500 on the season and have a road trip to Michigan following USC. Matt Campbell is straying to feel the heat and will rely on his defense to dig him out of this hole. PFF ranks Penn State’s defense sixth in the country overall, but they’ve given up 861 yards in the last two games. Penn State has forced four turnovers in that span but turned the ball over four times as well. Turnovers could be the storyline of the 2026 White Out. USC bounced back after the loss to Oregon with a close four-point win over Washington. The Huskies converted two fourth downs on their final drive before failing on 4th and 10 with a shot to the end zone. The Trojans defense had its best defensive effort against a P4 opponent this team with 198 yards allowed to Washington ‘s quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and held the Huskies to a 1-of-12 mark on third downs. Jayden Maiava had the fewest yards (245) and touchdowns (1) on the season versus Washington. Maiava was only sacked once, but you better believe Penn State will be bringing the pressure at home. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. away.blurb: Washington suffered a neck injury during spring practice and was due to be re-evaluated last week. Fisch said on Monday that it looks like the Huskies will not get the third-year runner back in action for a long while, however, so it's probably safe to assume that Washington is out for the season. Moss will not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a soft-tissue injury on the first play of the Washington State game. Chris Lawson has started three games in his absence at the X receiver position and is second on the team in receiving with 13 catches for 212 yards and a touchdown. Fisch said this week that their understanding is that Moss, a sixth-year senior, will be out of eligibility due to the NCAA eliminating injury waivers with the advent of 5-in-5 eligibility beginning this season. Carr will also not be re-evaluated until November 1 after suffering a hand injury against Washington State that required surgery. He had 5 carries for 28 yards before the injury, which opened the door for Limar to lead the Huskies backfield in the second half. With Carr, Limar, and Washington all out, freshman Brian Bonner Jr. and sixth-year Trey Cooley will continue to split reps in the Huskies backfield. Christian tore his Achilles during spring practice and is out for the season. He has remained around the team, but like Moss, will likely be out of eligibility after the year even with the injury wiping out his season. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night.
